title: Dated customs duty rules and route executability flags for gold and silver bars
howToUpdate: Add a new rule when a notification changes a rate; close the previous rule by setting its effectiveTo to the new rule's effectiveFrom (exclusive). Rates are decimals (0.10 = 10%). A null component means the split is not documented: the engine then uses the total rate and shows the split as PLACEHOLDER. Never enter 0 for an unknown rate.
coverageNote: Normal route covered from 2 Feb 2023. CEPA silver covered for FY2023-24, FY2024-25 and FY2026-27 only (FY2025-26 not located). CEPA gold quota covered from 2 Feb 2023. Dates without a rule return PLACEHOLDER.

rules.label: Budget 2023: bars 10% BCD + 5% AIDC
rules.note: Silver bars moved from 10.75% (7.5% BCD + 2.5% AIDC + 0.75% SWS) to 15%. Gold stayed at 15% with the split changed from 12.5% + 2.5% to 10% + 5%.

rules.label: CEPA-UAE silver, FY2023-24
rules.note: GTRI states 8% under CEPA against 15% MFN in FY2023-24. The CEPA schedule for that year was not located.

rules.label: CEPA-UAE silver, FY2024-25
rules.note: Reuters put the CEPA silver rate at 8% when the July 2024 cut took the normal rate to 6%.

rules.label: CEPA-UAE silver, FY2026-27 (unconfirmed)
rules.note: Reported as 7% by secondary sources in May 2026. The primary table (09/2026-Customs) was located but its silver row was not read; a one-point annual step-down from 8% in FY2024-25 would imply 6%. Whether AIDC applies on top is not confirmed.

rules.label: CEPA-UAE gold in-quota: 10% + 4% AIDC
rules.note: Sets CEPA Table III S.No. 12 to 10 (in-quota tariff) and 4 (in-quota AIDC). The row description was not quoted in the copy read; it is the gold row on strong inference (the same cells were set to 10/4 by 08/2023 and 4/1 by 31/2024).

exec.note: The standard import route used for the duty arithmetic. Channel conditions (who may import, and through which agency) are not modeled, and no executability document is cited.
The standard import route used for the duty arithmetic. Channel conditions (who may import, and through which agency) are not modeled, and no executability document is cited.
Silver bars (71069221, 71069229) moved from Free to Restricted for all origins. Export units, SEZs and jewellery-export schemes exempt.

Bars restricted; unwrought, powder and grain forms (71061000, 71069110/20/90) need a DGFT Import Authorisation, including through nominated agencies and IIBX. Refiners' dore under actual-user licence unchanged.
Reuters reported 939 tonnes of silver imported from the UAE in February 2024 while the paper wedge was open. Use is inferred from flows, not from quota or origin records.
UAE silver imports rose from US$29.2 million (FY2023) to US$1.74 billion (FY2024) while the paper wedge was open (GTRI). Use is inferred from flows, not from quota or origin records.
The July 2024 cut put the normal rate (6%) below the reported CEPA rate; Reuters reported that concessionary imports stopped. Executability itself is not documented.
Executability of the reopened wedge is not documented for these dates.
The DGFT curbs apply to the goods whatever their origin, so the CEPA paper rate does not by itself make the lane usable.
Tariff-rate quota; imports only through RBI- or DGFT-nominated agencies or IIBX qualified jewellers.
Tariff-rate quota; imports only through RBI- or DGFT-nominated agencies or IIBX qualified jewellers. FY2024-25 allocations were litigated (Delhi High Court, Jan 2025).
FY2025-26 quota permits extended to 30.09.2026 (DGFT Public Notice 18/2026-27).
FY2025-26 quota permits extended to 30.09.2026. No FY2026-27 allocation found in the gazette listings up to 25 Sep 2026.
FY2025-26 permits lapse after 30.09.2026 unless extended again. No FY2026-27 allocation was located as of 25 Sep 2026. Update this entry when DGFT publishes a notice.

execNote: Each entry has knowableFrom: the date its evidence was published. The replay shows an entry only from that date, so a flag cannot leak later evidence into an earlier step. The live tables use everything known today.
